intro: The JWT Decoder splits a JSON Web Token on its dots and base64url-decodes the header and payload into readable, pretty-printed JSON. It's handy when you need to inspect a bearer token's claims, algorithm, and expiry while debugging authentication flows. Note that it decodes only and does not verify the signature, so no secret or key is required.
useCases: Inspect the claims in a JWT, such as iss, sub, aud, exp, and iat, while debugging auth
Check the header to see which signing algorithm (alg) and key id (kid) a token uses
Confirm a token's expiry by reading the exp and iat timestamps in the payload
Quickly read a bearer token copied from a request header or login response
Decode tokens during local development without running a backend verification step

faq.q: Is my token sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Decoding runs entirely in your browser using built-in atob and TextDecoder APIs, so nothing is uploaded and the token never leaves your device.

faq.q: Does this verify the token's signature?
faq.a: No. It only decodes the header and payload; the signature is not checked and no secret or key is needed. A decoded payload does not mean the token is valid or trusted.

faq.q: What input format does it expect?
faq.a: A JWT in the standard header.payload.signature form, separated by dots. The decoder reads the first two parts (header and payload); at least two parts are required or it reports an invalid JWT.

faq.q: Why do I get an error on a valid-looking token?
faq.a: The header and payload must be valid base64url-encoded JSON. If a segment is truncated, malformed, or not JSON once decoded, parsing fails and an error is shown.

faq.q: Does it handle base64url encoding and padding?
faq.a: Yes. It converts the URL-safe characters (- and _) back to standard base64 and re-adds the missing = padding before decoding, so unpadded JWT segments work.
